newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Notionnel vol inches up, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Notionnel vol inches up, trade thin.

text.p: Implied volatility of notionnel options traded on MATIF ticked up slightly on Monday in very subdued holiday trade, dealers in Paris said.

"There is really very little going on," said one trader at a French house there. "We're waiting for tomorrow with the U.S. FOMC and then Thursday with the Bank of France and Buba -- they'll be the next events to provide any focus for the market."
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee is due to meet on Tuesday but dealers said the market was almost unanimous in expecting no change in interest rates
Also garnering some attention was Thursday's Bank of France repo tender results due around 1115 GMT and its regular fortnightly Monetary Policy Council meeting.
But perhaps the biggest event preoccupying markets was Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting, the first after the four-week summer recess.
Recent mark strength has fanned speculation of a near-term rise in German interest rates, though economists expected data due in the next few days to add weight to the "no chance" camp.
One trader quoted September at the money volatility for notionnel options at 5.0 percent, up from 4.20 percent at Thursday's close. The market was closed for Assumption Day on Friday.
He quoted October and December vol at 6.10 percent, up from 5.70 and 5.80 respectively.
"But it's very, very quiet, there's nothing going on," he said.
The French house trader noted limited call trading on the 130 September strike. By 1125 GMT, around 1,300 lots had traded.
The September notionnel future was up 0.10 at 129.64.
